title: Qluster Raises €4.7 Million Pre-Seed Round Led by Quantonation to Build Continuous-Variable Photonic Quantum Computers - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Paris-based photonic quantum computing startup Qluster has closed a €4.7 million ($5.18 million) pre-seed funding round led by Quantonation, with participation from Quantum Launchpad and Bpifrance. Spun out of France’s Laboratoire Kastler Brossel (LKB) (Sorbonne Université, CNRS, École normale supérieure, and Collège de France), the company will deploy the capital to establish an independent R&D laboratory and expand its experimental physics and quantum architecture teams.

Founded by Chief Executive Officer David Fainsin, Chief Technology Officer Ambroise Boyer, Chief Operating Officer Clarisse Thibault, and Chief Scientific Officer Valentina Parigi, Qluster builds on patented miniature multimode squeezed-light source technology developed by Parigi and Fainsin at LKB. Rather than encoding qubits in discrete single-photon paths, the platform uses continuous-variable (CV) cluster states across spectrally multiplexed optical modes at room temperature, aiming to eliminate cryogenic infrastructure and simplify data-center integration.

Alongside its optical hardware, Qluster employs an application-driven co-design methodology that maps target industrial workloads into circuit depth, logical qubit, and power budgets prior to finalizing processor topology. Previously backed by France 2030’s 2026 i-Lab Grand Prize as well as Agoranov, CNRS Innovation, and Sorbonne Université’s startup programs, the company targets an intermediate-scale quantum system by 2032 and a large-scale fault-tolerant universal processor by 2036.
